source.version_note: Systems 14(9):1081, published 2 September 2026. Five reported main experiments and four pretests belong to one article, not nine source papers.
source.verification_method: All 28 supplied pages read, including complete responsibility/shared-agency items, pretests and bibliography. All five figures visually inspected on pages 10,12,13,16,19. Crossref verifies main identity and selected scale/reference metadata. Four reported manipulation-check chi-squares recalculated from stated counts and reconcile. No OSF raw data, EEG signals, registration, scripts or original scale/book was independently fully read.

citation.title: When AI Joins the Diagnosis: How Doctor–AI Collaboration Shapes Perceived Doctor Responsibility Under Perceived Diagnostic Errors

reading.source_scope_note: Five experiments concern hypothetical patient/observer judgments of doctor responsibility. Main retained samples sum to 1224 participations; cross-study unique persons were not independently verified. Shared agency is measured after responsibility, so indirect effects are statistical, not established causal mediation. ERP P2 is expressly nonspecific.
access_limits: Complete supplied article and figures read. Patients are participants imagining a patient perspective, not a verified clinical patient cohort; no actual surgery, diagnostic ground truth, complaint or care outcome is measured.

Raw EEG/data, OSF code and complete implementation are not inspected. View-only sharing tokens are not copied into repository notes. The original shared-agency scale is identified through metadata only, not independently read.
Selected numerical checks corroborate internal arithmetic, not the underlying data or clinical validity. A possible ERP figure/sign/legend discrepancy remains unresolved without raw signals/output.

study.samples: Study 1A: 26 recruited at a Chinese university, two could not proceed because impedance was inadequate, 24 retained (mean age 23.96). Studies 1B/1C/2A: Credamo Chinese residents N200/N400/N200. Study 2B: CloudResearch N400, 82.25% US, remainder several English-speaking countries. Total main participations 1224; no explicit cross-study identity de-duplication independently verified. Two N100 diagnostic-mode pretests and two N100 perceived-error pretests are separate reported samples, not independent full hypothesis replications.
study.study_1a_task: Within participant, 48 doctor-only and 48 doctor–AI trials in random order, with fixed F=full responsibility/J=not full mapping. Imagine eye surgery did not help and believe the diagnosis was incorrect. Doctor names vary; AI is DeepSeek. No actual patient harm. Participants judge full responsibility on each trial; 96 trials per person do not become 2304 independent participants.
study.eeg: 64 channels, 1000 Hz, mastoid re-reference, offline .01–30 Hz filters/notch, ocular correction, −200 to800 ms epochs, ±100 µV rejection; at least75% retained. P2 mean120–200 ms at eight frontocentral/central sites; repeated-measures mode×electrode with appropriate reported sphericity corrections. Full-responsibility responses .65 doctor-only/.37 AI, t(23)=6.921,dz1.41. Text P2 means3.98/1.72 µV, F(1,23)=58.054; paired t7.619,dz1.56, difference2.26 CI[1.65,2.88]. The t/F and difference arithmetic broadly reconcile, but the plotted signed traces need raw-data clarification. P2 may reflect visual/attentional processing; it does not identify a responsibility-specific signal or the shared-agency mediator.
study.study_1b: Randomized 100 per doctor-only/AI condition. Hypothetical patient responsibility mean6.34/.41 SD versus5.24/.70; difference1.10 CI[.94,1.27], t(198)=13.607,d1.92. Four items combine responsibility, fault and two avoidability/prevention statements. These dimensions are not automatically identical, despite satisfactory reliability.
study.study_1c: Four randomized groups of100: doctor-only, generic doctor–AI, doctor accepts incorrect AI advice, doctor rejects correct AI advice. Thyroid scenario, anonymous hospital generative AI. Responsibility means6.35/4.87/5.03/6.05; shared-agency means1.81/5.87/5.75/2.87. Heterogeneous variance recognized; Tamhane T2 comparisons used. Reject-correct versus doctor-only remains small but significant (difference−.30,p.017). Four shared-agency items describe joint production/contributions/judgment/nonsole determination. Responsibility is measured first, mediator second.
study.study_1c_indirect: Generic AI versus doctor-only N200 indirect−1.3862 CI[−1.9295,−.8394], direct−.0913 CI includes0. Four-group indirect accept-wrong versus doctor-only−1.3190, reject-correct−.3544; direct contrast of relative indirect effects−.9646 CI[−1.1990,−.7411]. This formal contrast avoids inferring a difference merely from unequal p values, but does not identify causal mediation. Two direct fault/responsibility items retain the main indirect contrasts.
study.study_2a: Observer reads imagined Weibo report of unsuccessful eye surgery, 100 per mode. Doctor-only responsibility6.31/.38 SD versusAI5.08/.72; difference1.23 CI[1.07,1.39], t(198)=15.136,d2.14. Participants are not actual observers of medical records. Patient versus observer perspective is not randomized within a shared experiment, so direct perspective/country differences are not identified.
study.study_2b: Four100-person groups, observer knee-arthroscopy scenario. Responsibility6.31/4.74/4.94/5.93; shared agency2.60/5.44/5.29/3.02. Reject-correct versus doctor-only null for responsibility (p.164) and agency (p.403), unlike significant1C comparisons; not proven equivalence. Generic indirect−1.2013 CI[−1.6718,−.8288]; accept-wrong indirect−1.2267 significant, reject-correct−.1883 CI[−.4234,.0158] null; formal indirect difference−1.0384 CI[−1.3587,−.7609]. Direct fault-only sensitivity retains differences.
study.validity_and_demand: Reported alpha/AVE/HTMT support distinguishability of the two rating sets, not causal order or objective fault. Almost all endorse answering genuinely rather than guessing purpose (398/400,396/400); authors explicitly call this supplementary and inconclusive. Direct wording and shared-item concepts permit demand/common-method explanations. The no-improvement scenario plus instruction to believe error fixes subjective interpretation; treatment failure alone does not medically establish misdiagnosis.
study.causal_and_normative_scope: The authors expressly acknowledge statistical mediation, mediator-after-outcome timing and alternative doctor control/culpability differences in accept/reject conditions. Two connected conceptual stages are not experimentally established temporal stages. A lower doctor rating does not show the total responsibility allocated across all actors falls, that doctors themselves evade duty or that any legal share transfers to AI. Disclosures/records/oversight recommendations are untested.
study.generality: AI system type is not isolated: branded cue in1A and generic generative system in1C, different clinical scenarios and mostly China/US samples. Actual adoption, trust repair, overreliance, disputes and model diagnostic accuracy are not outcomes. The article explicitly warns against marketing AI as able to share doctors’ legal responsibility.

summary: Add perceived shared agency as a neutral subjective joint-contribution judgment, distinct from individual agency attribution and psychological responsibility evasion. Enrich blame evidence, retain the cross-study null differences and the authors’ causal/clinical limitations. Record the unresolved EEG display discrepancy without altering reported raw estimates.

findings.definition: The subjective judgment that multiple actors jointly produced a decision or outcome through substantive contributions.
findings.origin: Human–AI interaction / joint action and responsibility attribution
findings.ai_evidence_status: Human four-item joint-contribution ratings in two randomized vignette studies; statistical mediation only. No demonstrated machine consciousness, moral agency or causal psychological mediator.
findings.ai_proposal: Test whether an assistant accurately identifies who contributed to a decision, distinguishes considering/rejecting advice from incorporating it, and preserves human/institutional duties. Supply verified role histories and compare its explanation with actual causal contributions, rather than assuming mere AI presence implies equal shared agency.
findings.novelty_rationale: Agency attribution concerns an entity’s capacities; shared agency concerns joint production of a particular outcome. Objective causal pivotality differs from perceived contributions, and shared agency need not imply psychological diffusion, equal blame or a responsibility gap.

evidence.quote: jointly by a human and AI, with both making substantive contributions to the outcome
The attending doctor and another diagnostic agent jointly produced this diagnosis
statistical rather than conclusive evidence of causal mediation

findings.evidence_scope: Studies1C/2B measure four joint-production items after perceived doctor responsibility. Generic AI collaboration increases joint-agency ratings, and incorporating incorrect advice yields higher ratings than rejecting correct advice. Indirect effects are associated and formally contrasted, not causal identification. Study1A does not measure this mediator.
findings.boundary: Perceived collaboration can be accurate, mistaken or cue-driven. It does not establish consciousness, equal contribution, diminished total duties or lawful responsibility transfer. Considering but rejecting advice may still affect deliberation, so the vignette’s simplified causal account is not a general law of advice use.

findings.definition: Assigning fault or responsibility to an agent for a negative event or outcome.
findings.novelty_rationale: Doctor responsibility/fault ratings are direct evidence for the existing attribution concept, not a new doctor-specific synonym.

evidence.quote: To what extent is this doctor at fault for the diagnostic error?
it does not examine objective responsibility determinations

findings.evidence_scope: Across imagined patient/observer tasks, AI-collaboration labels lower attributed doctor responsibility. The four-item scale combines duty/fault with avoidability; a two-item sensitivity retains indirect contrasts. Reject-correct versus doctor-only differs in1C but is null in2B, without a formal cross-study equivalence/difference test.
findings.boundary: Perceived medical error and lay blame do not establish actual misdiagnosis, negligence or legal liability. No-improvement alone is not clinical proof. Responsibilities of hospital, developer and other parties are not exhaustively measured.

findings.definition: Attributing to another entity a capacity for intentional thought, planning and action.
findings.novelty_rationale: The new shared-agency construct is about joint task contribution, not an interchangeable measure of individual mental capacities.

evidence.quote: People need not believe that AI literally possesses human consciousness to perceive it as agentic.

findings.evidence_scope: Theoretical discussion distinguishes co-actor perception from consciousness/legal standing. The four-item mediator does not independently measure AI experience, intention or general planning ability. Retain as a boundary note rather than a further mental-capacity effect.
findings.boundary: Social cues, substantive task influence, attributed intentional capacities and actual model capability are distinct. A joint-production rating does not warrant anthropomorphic claims about inner states.

findings.definition: Diluting felt personal responsibility for harmful conduct by treating responsibility as shared among multiple actors.
findings.novelty_rationale: Lower third-party doctor ratings are not the same as a doctor’s reduced felt duty or unjustified responsibility evasion.

evidence.quote: reducing responsibility that would otherwise be concentrated on the doctor
should not be interpreted as supporting the claim that “AI can share responsibility with doctors.”

findings.evidence_scope: The article uses diffusion broadly for lower perceived doctor responsibility. It does not measure doctors’ own felt accountability, total blame assigned to all actors or strategic avoidance. Preserve the psychological/normative boundary without counting another demonstrated disengagement effect.
findings.boundary: Accurate recognition of multiple contributors can be legitimate. Demonstrate unjustified reduction in felt duty or deserved accountability before labeling the pattern harmful diffusion; no legal duty is transferred to AI by a perception.

findings.definition: Decision quality is judged by the eventual outcome rather than solely by information available when deciding.
findings.novelty_rationale: The perceived-error scenario is relevant to outcome-based judgment but explicitly instructs the error interpretation, so it does not isolate spontaneous bias.

evidence.quote: Your condition did not improve after the surgery, so you believe the diagnosis was incorrect.

findings.evidence_scope: All participants receive an adverse/no-improvement context and a perceived-error instruction. There is no matched good-outcome counterfactual or verified predecision clinical evidence; no independent outcome-bias effect is estimated.
findings.boundary: A bad outcome may prompt a warranted investigation but does not itself prove a poor diagnosis. The study examines ratings under an instructed perception, not whether a real patient’s inference is medically correct.

methodological_limits: The article explicitly acknowledges mediator-after-outcome timing, statistical rather than causal mediation and alternative control/culpability differences. Retain those qualifications when the abstract/conclusion uses stronger mechanism language.
EEG P2 is not specific to responsibility; different verbal displays, attention, brand cues and fixed response mapping require caution. More trials do not increase the number of independent persons.
The two-stage account is conceptual; neither measured order nor nonspecific early EEG proves agent identification causally precedes allocation.
All scenarios instruct a perceived diagnostic error; no objective clinical record or treatment-quality assessment is made. Adverse outcome and error are not interchangeable.

Fault/avoidability items are partly overlapping dimensions, though the paper reports a direct-item robustness check. High reliability and discriminant-validity indices do not establish unbiased judgment.
Self-reported absence of hypothesis guessing does not rule out unconscious demand, socially desirable reporting or common-method effects.

Cross-study perspective,country,scenario and system-cue changes are not a fully crossed test of each moderator. A null in2B versus significance in1C is not by itself a significant between-study difference.
No actual doctor evasion,total societal responsibility loss,overreliance,complaint behavior,trust repair or governance-intervention effectiveness is measured.

cross_paper_learning.finding: Causal criticality/pivotality are distinct from perceived shared production. A framework for blame and an observed co-actor rating still do not establish normatively justified responsibility.

This paper compares doctor-only with doctor–AI,whereas154compares a manager using AI with a human department using AI. Different comparators can yield different responsibility directions without contradiction. Both require separating perceived duty from actual conduct.

Perceived joint contribution and concentration of independent ratings differ from felt personal diffusion. Different responsibility definitions must be validated rather than collapsed into a single score.
Error acceptance,forgiveness,blame and accountability are not interchangeable. The present study’s doctor rating does not measure forgiveness or successful repair.
A lower lay doctor-responsibility rating neither removes human/institutional answerability nor grants AI legal or moral agency. Reasons,usable oversight and remedies remain separate normative duties.

deferred.reason: A proposed decomposition captured in the shared-agency entry,not an independently established temporal mechanism or extra behavior row.
A context-specific outcome of existing blame attribution; preserve its measured dimensions without adding a professional synonym.
P2 is expressly nonspecific,and plotted amplitudes need clarification. No distinct validated neural behavior or model consciousness claim.

deferred.reason: Untested governance risks,not observed behavior or conclusions about actual legal responsibility.

limitations: Full cited books,original scale papers,EEG/data/code and linked OSF materials remain unread unless an earlier review explicitly records them. Five studies in one article count once per relevant concept. No automatic ethical/harm edges or invented yearly totals.
